startup.name: BlindPay
startup.description: Stablecoin API that lets companies send and receive money worldwide using fiat, stablecoins and several blockchains, with the compliance and regulatory work handled by the provider. Nine person team in San Francisco, Winter 2025.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting prior about 1 percent (0.6 to 2 percent range). Up for a nine person team, a payments need that is clear and timing with rising stablecoin interest, and for a developer product in an API format that YC often funds. Down because the space has funded rivals and a compliance wrapped crypto pitch. Net about 4 percent, conditional on the batch already given.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say that stablecoin payment APIs are a crowded field with funded leaders such as Bridge and BVNK, and that a compliance wrapper depends on partners the company does not control. Partners may also want proof of live payment volume instead of a regulatory plan.

Time table Fintech: seed median 7 months, series_a median 26.5, series_b median 42.8 from batch start.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 22.4 months from 2025-01-06 to 2026-11-17 and the number is for a round above about 1M from outside investors inside that window, not ever. Anchors are 0.57 for Fintech 2022 to 2025 and 0.70 for payments (n=10). 0.55 is 0.96x of the Fintech anchor. The 22 month window covers nearly every eventual seed, since the p75 for Fintech is 20 months. A team of 9 and a hot stablecoin theme are not lifted above the anchor, per the winners test. These odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under 3M, the most common outcome for a small team that closes a first outside round quickly.
Institutional seed near the 2022 and later YC median of 4.1M, with market pre money near 18M.
Strong seed led by a known fund, matching the upper quartile of 6.5M and above in press covered rounds.
Large hot category round; rare for a team this early.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed step fails if licensing and banking partners slow launch, so volume stays too small to show an investor, or if the product looks like a thin layer over providers such as Bridge and BVNK. Meson and Peg, earlier stablecoin YC companies, both shut down, and Koywe and Coco Wallet stayed small after early rounds. A crypto flavoured pitch can also narrow the investor pool.

bands.rationale: Small or slow Series A below the 2022 and later p25 of 10M.
Typical Series A near the 2022 and later YC median of 14.15M and a market deal size near 17M.
Upside round after fast revenue growth; the p75 is about 20M.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A inside 22 months needs a visible stream of processed payment volume and clean compliance in several corridors, while larger rivals compete on price. Verto took two years from seed to A, and NALA took five, so stablecoin API peers usually need several years of volume growth before an institutional A.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B inside 22 months would need payments volume at scale and licensing across regions, which took Verto and NALA far longer. Regulation of stablecoin intermediaries can also freeze a launch, and a 9 person team would still be proving a single product line.

bands.rationale: Smaller later round near the 2022 and later p25 of 35M (n=9 only).
Typical Series C or later, 45M to 77M per the YC table and market monitor.
Breakout late round at unicorn scale; very rare in this cohort.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C inside two years of YC is almost unseen among payments companies, whose own scale of regulated volume takes many years to build. The best known cross border payments peers such as NALA and Verto were still at Series A at comparable ages, so near zero is the honest figure.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The most common ending is a quiet stall or a small acquisition by a larger payments or exchange firm, the path of Consul and Cypher. Big upside needs to become a top rail among rivals who raised tens of millions earlier, as the NALA and Verto stories show it takes many years.

technical_complexity.rationale: The API itself is straightforward, but chain integrations, custody, KYC and banking partners are the hard part, and a small team can build a first corridor in months. The moat is licences and partner relationships, which are slow, not model quality.

takeover_risk.rationale: Large payments firms already ship stablecoin APIs and have licences and distribution. A new entrant must differentiate on compliance depth or a region.

evidence.claim: Corporates cite cross border supplier payments as the top stablecoin use, and surveys report cost savings of 10 percent or more.
B2B accounts for most real stablecoin payment volume per industry reports.

roadmap.proof: Volume growing monthly with retained customers.

weaknesses: Blind suggests opacity to a compliance buyer
brand.rationale: A compound that names the category is easy to remember like Rappi style names are not, but for a compliance buyer the word blind may raise a question about transparency. Brand is secondary here.

narrative.headline: A nine person stablecoin API team in a crowded, licence heavy space: seed is roughly a coin flip over 22 months, later rounds are unlikely in the window.
narrative.general_summary: BlindPay offers a stablecoin API for global payments with the compliance work handled for clients. The window is 22.4 months from 2025-01-06 to 2026-11-17, which covers nearly all eventual seeds, so seed sits at 0.55 against Fintech and payments anchors of 0.57 and 0.70. Series A given seed is 0.10 in the window. Funded rivals and licensing are the main drags. Earlier stablecoin YC companies Meson and Peg shut down, while Verto and NALA took years to reach a Series A, which is why the later rounds are priced low for a window under two years. The odds do not rank this company against others.
